newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch flower auction handles record 190 mln flowers.
newsitem.headline: Dutch flower auction handles record 190 mln flowers.

text.p: Aalsmeer flower auction handled a record 190 million flowers in the run up to Mothers' Day on May 11, a spokeswoman from the auction said.
Mothers' Day in the Netherlands, Germany, Belgium and Luxembourg is this weekend and turnover in the past week was 10 percent up on last year, she added.
In an average week at Aalsmeer, only half that number amount of flowers would be handled, she said.
The flowers are produced in the Netherlands and other countries such as Israel as well as Kenya, Zimbabwe, she said.

Although many countries in Europe celebrate May 11 as Mothers Day, exceptions are the Britain, Spain and Hungary which celebrated on May 4 and France which celebrates at the end of the month on May 25.
"It has been incredibly busy at the auction and everyone works around the clock, even through public holidays," she said.

Earlier today ,the International Union of Food and Agricultural Workers(IUF) said in Geneva that labour and environmental abuses in poorer countries were widespread in the rapidly expanding global flower industry.

It added that although the flower trade in Europe had launched various forms of "eco labelling" to meet growing environmental awareness among consumers, some of these did not even conform to minimum international labour standards.

The report said that developing countries now hold over 25 percent of the world trade in flowers, which is heavily reliant on the airline industry for quick delivery to the major markets in the U.S., Europe and Japan.
It added the EU was the leading importer of flowers, over 21 percent of which -- to a value of $519 million in 1995 -- came from poorer countries, mainly in Latin America and Africa.
